text:
katie: quick heads-up — we'll start a targeted schema slimming for console telemetry next week. goal: remove/normalize two high-cardinality route metadata attrs that blow up our columnar storage and p99 query times.

darren: which attrs exactly? and are we talking dual-write or in-place backfill?

katie: route_labels_v2 (jsonb) and route_tag_history (text array). both are rarely used by console queries but are heavy for analytics scans. plan is: 1) add route_labels_ref (int) as an indirection, 2) lightweight lookup table route_labels_dedup(id, payload), 3) dual-write ingest -> both old fields and new ref, 4) gradual backfill + canary queries.

priya: hmm do we have a cardinality estimate for route_labels_v2? last sample showed ~12M distinct payloads/month, but 95% are one-offs. dedup table should collapse to ~150k rows.

aleks: sounds good. what about console dashboards that currently do jsonb->>'owner' pattern? they'll break if we remove jsonb. need a compatibility layer in the query adaptor.

katie: yes, plan includes a small read-adapter in console: when route_labels_v2 exists, prefer new join on route_labels_dedup, otherwise fallback to jsonb extraction. we'll gate via feature flag.

darren: migration timeline? and SLOs? need an ops plan for backfill - we can't spike IO.

katie: timeline proposal: week1 dual-write + feature-flagged reads; week2 small backfill sampling on a subset of tenants (canary); week3 full backfill with rate limit; week4 flip flag and drop old columns after observing metrics for 2 weeks.

priya: backfill approach: do chunked id-range jobs with a sidecar that checks current ingest parity. sample SQL below for the dedup insert/lookup:

```sql
with v as (select distinct route_labels_v2 as payload from telemetry_queue where route_labels_v2 is not null limit 100000)
insert into route_labels_dedup (payload) select payload from v on conflict (payload) do nothing returning id;

-- later update telemetry events to set route_labels_ref = r.id from route_labels_dedup r where telemetry_queue.route_labels_v2 = r.payload;
```

aleks: need to ensure route_labels_dedup has compact hash idx and a TTL/retention policy for pathologic churn. also encrypt payload? contains PII?

katie: payloads are small dicts, some users put emails — we should run a quick PII check and then add a redaction hook. for now flag as sensitive; KMS encryption on the dedup table is an ops requirement.

darren: what about route_tag_history array? simpler: normalize to a separate table route_tag_events(route_id, tag, ts) and keep compressed rollup for console when needed. avoid expanding arrays inline in telemetry.

priya: agree. console queries that do array overlap will change semantics: we'll provide a compatibility UDF that returns the same result for a while, but warn in release notes.

ingest-bot: deploy plan created: https://ci/internal/plan/TELE-1243. dual-write microservice branch: jobs/telemetry-dualwrite-2026.

katie: perf gating: we will monitor console p99, analytics scan throughput, and storage delta. key metric: bytes_scanned_per_query and route_label_lookup_miss_rate. set alerts at +15% on scan bytes and >0.1% lookup miss.

aleks: one more ops edge: queries that use route_labels_v2 as a filter in materialized views — will need MV rewrite. we should produce a migration map listing all affected MVs and dashboards.

darren: i'll run an automated search across dashboards and saved queries for jsonb keys and generate the map. ETA EOD.

katie: thanks. action items: @darren generate dashboard map; @priya draft backfill job with chunk sizing; @aleks create dedup table schema + encryption plan; i'll wire feature flag and rally canary tenants. we will sync tomorrow 10am. :rocket:

priya: quick question — for backfill idempotency: use a job that writes route_labels_ref and records progress in job_checkpoint table?

katie: yes, checkpoint per tenant and shard. job should be resumable and safe to rerun.

darren: noted. i'll post the dashboard map when ready.

ingest-bot: canary cluster usage quota: scheduled 2h nightly windows for backfill jobs to avoid contention.

katie: perfect. thanks all.
